evidence: All tested QNNs trail matched controls by 10.9-16.7 pp; held-out confirmation hit RAM floor; scale-up unjustified.

hypothesis: Distinct three-class quantum-kernel or fixed-reservoir families may complement supervised QNN.
evidence: Existing kernel/reservoir implementations address the binary target and underperformed their matched controls. Three-class QNN variants also trail matched classical controls; resources are constrained. No three-class extension was justified.

hypothesis: Accumulate exact full-batch gradients in small chunks to lower peak memory without changing optimizer updates.
evidence: One-step, six-row comparison: chunk size 2 matched full-batch loss within 2.3e-16, circuit weights within 2.4e-12, readout within 7e-18; both used six circuit executions. On resume, raw RAM was 853 MiB before QML imports; safe 700 MiB post-import headroom could not be established, so the 36-origin confirmation was not launched.
